top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, KLOwen, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, Lightforce, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, SLB, herbst expanders, owen crotty
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, rentability, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, practice optimisation, staff efficiency, diary changes, scheduling, dynamic scheduling, emergencies decrease, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements, practice efficiencies, performance in NHS Hospital environment
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save them time or money, or that it will reduce the number of in-person appointments. They question whether the investment in DM will pay off in terms of efficiency, profitability, or staff workload, especially for braces cases.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Evidence that DM reduces number of visits for braces cases
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Resources that explore the benefits of self-ligating bracket monitoring and using insights with braces
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific ROI and efficiency data, especially for braces and mixed appliance practices. Comparative studies versus standard recall protocols and real-world cost-benefit analyses are most lacking.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI for clinical observations and remote monitoring
top_needs.brands_and_products: SmartSTL, Damon, Spark, Invisalign, self-ligating braces
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of scanning, occlusal assessment, class I goal, passivity archwires, AI efficiency, FDA class I, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, aligner unseat tracking
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI is accurate enough to reliably detect clinical changes, diagnose remotely, or replace in-person assessments. Some are concerned about regulatory validation and the ability to trust AI-driven decisions.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
How accurate is SmartSTL AI
top_needs.gap_assessment: More peer-reviewed, quantitative studies on AI accuracy for specific clinical tasks and regulatory validation (e.g., FDA) are needed. Evidence for AI performance in diverse populations and appliances is limited.
